raw_response:
*Reasoning in my own voice:*

Aiya, where do I start. My piece of land is 8.2 mu, not much. About 6 mu I do wheat-maize back to back like most folks in our village, and the other 2.2 mu I keep in cotton — that's the corner near the road, drains better. My old man went to the city again this year, he does construction work, so it's mostly me in the field. My daughter-in-law helps when she's not minding the little one. My son also works outside. Five mouths in the house but only me really doing the farming.

The wheat I already put in last October, middle of the month, when the cool air came. I planted same as always — broke up the ground with the rotovator (paid my nephew, he has the machine), put down compound fertilizer before sowing, that dark bag from the agro-shop in town with the three numbers. About one bag per mu. The seed I just buy whatever they have, I don't know the names, I trust the shopkeeper, he's known us a long time. Now it's spring and the wheat is greening up nicely. In a few days I'll spread urea — about 20 jin per mu [10 kg/mu], everyone in the village does this around now. If the rain doesn't come I'll have to turn on the well — water costs money, the meter runs, I have to pay the electricity. Usually I water three times: when it stands up [jointing], when the heads come out, and once more when the grain is filling if it's dry. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu [400 kg/mu], I'll be happy with the same.

When wheat is cut in early June there's no time to rest — have to plant maize right away, within a few days, or it gets too late and the cold catches it in autumn. My nephew comes again with the rotovator, just one shallow pass, then we plant by hand with the little pusher-planter, my daughter-in-law on one row and me on the other. I put compound fertilizer in with the seed when planting. Later, when the maize is up to my waist, I scatter urea between the rows, maybe 20 jin per mu. Maize doesn't need much water in our area — the summer rains usually come. Last year I only had to water it once. Got about 900 jin per mu [450 kg/mu], pretty normal.

The cotton — I've grown cotton my whole life, my mother grew cotton, this is what women here do. I plant end of April when the ground is warm. The 2.2 mu I keep is plowed proper, deeper than the wheat ground. I put compound and a little urea when planting, then more urea when the buds come. Cotton is so much trouble — bollworm, aphids, you have to spray, four or five times through summer. And the picking, ai, the picking takes weeks, you go bit by bit as the bolls open, fingers get sore. I do most of it myself in the cool morning, daughter-in-law helps a few days. Last year about 250 jin lint per mu [125 kg/mu], price was decent. Why do I still grow cotton? Because I know how, and I can pick it without buying any machine. Some neighbors quit cotton, it's true, but for me on these 2.2 mu it works.

This year my worry is money. Fertilizer is dear, the diesel for the pump is dear, everything is dear. So I have to be careful. I will not buy more than I can pay for. If by the time of summer urea I'm short, I'll skip the second top-dress on the maize and pray for good rain. That's how it is.
